  payment. How much should it be paid?

  ago when the interest rate was 4.06% per year. ₹5,000 was borrowed three years ago at 3.42%. Two  
  years ago, she borrowed ₹6,000 at 5.23%, and last year ₹7,000 was borrowed at 6.03% per year. Now  
  she would like to consolidate her debt into a single 20-year loan with a 6% fixed annual interest rate. If  
  Ashea makes annual payments (starting in one year) to repay her total debt, what is the amount of each

  2A)   A company acquired specialized equipment for \$1,950, anticipating it would retain a salvage value of  
  \$450 after a 5-year useful life. To analyse depreciation impact on financial statements, calculate and  
  present a detailed depreciation schedule using the following two approaches:                             (4)  
  a) If the company adopts the Straight-Line depreciation method.  
  b) If the company uses the Double Declining Balance method.  
  
  2B)   An industrial firm is considering two processes for manufacturing storm drains.                          (3)  
  Plan 1 (conventional injection moulding): It requires a initial cost of \$2,000,000. The cost for  
  inspecting, maintaining, and cleaning the moulds is expected to be \$ 6000 per year. The cost of  
  materials for this plan is expected to be the same as for the other plan.  
  Plan 2 (virtual engineered composites): The first cost to tool the floating mould is only \$27,000.  
  However, because of the newness of the process, personnel and product-reject costs are expected to be  
  higher than those for a conventional process. The company expects the operating costs to be \$46,000  
  per year for the first 8 years and then to decrease to \$11,000 per year thereafter.  
  At an interest rate of 10% per year, which process should the company select based on present worth  
  analysis over a 14-year study period?
